 Judgment
EASWARAN S., J.
The State of Kerala are the appellants.
The appeal is directed against the judgment and decree in LAR No.3 of 2014 of the Sub Court, Kottayam.
Ares of land comprised in Survey No.600/3-1 of Kaduthuruthi Village of Vaikom Taluk was acquired for the construction of Kadathuruthi Bye-pass.
Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act notification was dated 01.01.2011.
As per award No.4/2013(12) dated 25.03.2013 the Land Acquisition Officer awarded the land value at Rs.56,626/- per Are thereby including the property under category C - Wetland.
The Land Acquisition Officer relied on the basic document Sale Deed No.1279/2008 dated 12.05.2008 for fixing the value at Rs.56,626/-.
Aggrieved by the fixation of the land value, the claimant preferred LAR No.3/2014.

The reference was taken up for consideration along with a batch of cases and the Sub Court categorized the properties into four and fixed the value in accordance with the importance of the land falling under each category.

3. While fixing the land value, the reference Court found that the property of the claimants/respondents were liable to be included in category C and thereby fixed the land value at Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two lakh fifty thousand only) per cent and [Rs.6,17,500/-(Rupees Six lakh seventeen thousand five hundred only) per Are].

Accordingly, the compensation amount was fixed at Rs.33,96,250/- (Rupees Thirty three lakh ninety six thousand two hundred and fifty only)
(6,17,500 x 5.5).
Aggrieved by the above fixation of the land value, the State of Kerala has come up in the present appeal.

sentences.text: The present Land Acquisition Appeal was heard along with a batch of appeal by a Division Bench of this Court by judgment dated 11.10.2023, the land value fixed by the reference court for the category A to D were revised.

However, after pronouncing the judgment in the present appeal it was brought to the notice of the Court that the sole respondent expired and accordingly the judgment was recalled and the appeal was listed thereafter.

5. When the matter came up for consideration today, we have allowed the application for impleading the legal heirs of the respondent claimant and Registry has been directed to carry out the necessary corrections in the cause title of the appeal.
6. In our considered view, we need not delve upon the minute facts which is stated in the appeal, nor we are required to consider the rival contentions raised by the parties in the appeal threadbare.

In our considered view the point raised is covered by the judgment of the Division Bench in L.A.App.
No.521 of 2015 and connected cases.

Relevant paragraph of the aforesaid judgment is hereby extracted:
".....23.
C-Category properties are reclaimed lands but have access to Panchayat road.
D- Category properties are also reclaimed lands.
These lands have a more notable disadvantage that there is no road access.
Therefore, value of D-Category properties would be much lesser than C-Category properties, which have road access.

Having regard to all such aspects, we are of the view that the value of lands in C and D categories are liable to be fixed by scaling down by 10% and 25% respectively from the value of B category lands.

Accordingly, the market value of the acquired lands in Categories A, B, C and D are refixed as follows,-
 Category Value per Are

B Rs.5,99,100/-
 C Rs.5,39,190/-
 D Rs.4,49,325/-
These appeals are allowed to the above extent.

The claimants are entitled to compensation computing the land value at the said rates along with all statutory benefits."
7.

A reading of the afore extracted paragraph of the judgment in LAA No.521 of 2015 and connected cases reveals that as against the fixation of Rs.6,17,500/- (Rupees Six lakh seventeen thousand five hundred only) per Are in respect of properties covered under category C fixed by the reference court,
the Division Bench of this Court has refixed the same at Rs.5,39,190/- (Rupees Five lakh thirty nine thousand one hundred and ninety only).
